question: In which different parts do the plants store their waste products?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Leaves, vacuoles and Old xylem**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Plants store their waste products in **leaves, vacuoles, and old xylem**.
 
• These parts help in isolating the waste substances from the living cells and tissues, thereby protecting the plant from potential damage.
 
• **Leaves** often accumulate waste products which are eventually shed off during leaf fall.
 
• **Vacuoles** are cellular organelles that store various substances, including waste products, in a plant cell.
 
• **Old xylem**, also known as heartwood, stores waste products which contribute to its dark color and density.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Plants produce a variety of waste products as a result of m**etabolic activities.**
 
• In addition to **leaves, vacuoles, and old xylem, some plants also excrete waste** products through their roots or secrete them into the soil.
 
• Some waste products are also stored in **specialized structures like resin ducts or laticifers.**
 
• These mechanisms help the plant to manage and dispose of waste efficiently, ensuring healthy growth and development.
